title: Battery Pack Health Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: Wear down four AA batteries in series and see how the falling pack voltage slows the robot's motors and puts the RP2040 board at risk of resetting.

educational.topic: Battery voltage, motor speed, and microcontroller brownout
learningObjectives: Calculate the voltage of four AA cells connected in series from the voltage of one cell
Analyze how a falling pack voltage lowers motor speed for a fixed PWM duty command
Identify the pack voltage below which the RP2040 board is at risk of resetting
Decide what to check first when a physical robot drives slowly or restarts unexpectedly
prerequisites: Voltage as the push that moves electric charge (Chapter 1: Voltage and Current)
Four 1.5 V AA batteries in series make 6 V (Chapter 1: Your Battery Pack)

controls.label: Wear down over time
controls.purpose: Drain the batteries by 1% per second

assumptions: Cell voltage falls linearly with charge
Motor speed is proportional to the voltage the motor driver receives
limitations: Real alkaline discharge curves are not linear
The exact reset threshold depends on the board's voltage regulator

keyQuestions: If each battery drops to 1.2 V, what is the pack voltage and how fast does the robot drive?
What is the highest charge at which the board first shows Reset risk?
Why does the half-speed command halve the speed but not change the reset risk?
Your real robot drives slowly and sometimes restarts. What do you check first?
commonMisconceptions: Batteries are either full or dead, with nothing in between
A slow robot always means a bug in the code
Lowering the PWM duty cycle protects the board from low-battery resets
assessmentOpportunities: Record pack voltage, motor speed and board status at 20% charge intervals
Find and justify the 35% reset-risk threshold using the formula
Exit ticket linking voltage, motor speed and resets
